html:
Finnmark is the far north of Norway, on the Arctic coast beyond the tree line. The map shows it from 1600 to 1800, the years when its borders were still in dispute.

It is part of the homeland of the Sami; old Norse writers called the Sami "Finns", which gave the region its name. Norwegians lived in fishing villages along the coast, and the crown held the fortress of Vardøhus at Vardø. Inland, the Sami followed reindeer and paid taxes to more than one ruler at once, since Denmark-Norway, Sweden and Russia all claimed them.

Rivalry over the far north helped cause the Kalmar War between Denmark-Norway and Sweden in 1611. In the 1600s Vardø also held some of the harshest witch trials in Scandinavia. Russian traders from the White Sea, the Pomors, came each summer to buy fish. The border with Sweden was fixed in 1751 and the border with Russia only in 1826.
